item.text:
**Bottom Line**
Mixed, but leaning **no**. In 2024 Xi’s economic record shows real technocratic policy work and some pro-growth appointments, but the clearest institutional evidence points to **more Party control over economic decision-making**, not empowered autonomous professionals. I found **no credible 2024 evidence** that Xi elevated family members or business partners into top economic roles.

| Direction | Claim-level item | Publisher | Date | URL | QIDs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| For | Xi’s finance ministry pushed a broad-based growth agenda: more investment in equipment renewal, consumer trade-ins, fair treatment for all firms in tax relief/procurement, and more funding for education, healthcare, social security, and environmental protection. | Xinhua / english.www.gov.cn | 2024-03-25 | https://english.www.gov.cn/news/202403/25/content_WS6600afebc6d0868f4e8e569e.html | 5B.2, 5B.1 |
| For | The NDRC said it would keep helping private enterprises, protect entrepreneurs’ rights, and use private-sector feedback as an input to macro policy, which is consistent with a competence-and-feedback model rather than pure patronage. | Xinhua / english.news.cn | 2024-01-10 | https://english.news.cn/20240110/78198229d70d4ad2824f8b50c3bedeee/c.html | 5B.2, 5B.1 |
| For | IMF staff said China’s authorities were focusing on innovation, green/high-tech sectors, and mitigating property/local-government risks, but still needed a “comprehensive” reform package for high-quality and sustainable growth. | IMF | 2024-08-02 | https://www.imf.org/en/publications/cr/issues/2024/08/01/peoples-republic-of-china-2024-article-iv-consultation-press-release-staff-report-and-552803 | 5B.2, 5B.1 |
| Mixed | The central bank reshuffled its monetary policy committee to include CSRC head Wu Qing and two academically trained economists, which is technocratic on its face, but Reuters also noted the panel’s influence is limited and the PBOC lacks real independence. | Reuters | 2024-03-19 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy/chinas-central-bank-reshuffles-monetary-policy-committee-3345182 | 5B.2 |
| Against | China revised the State Council Organic Law to give the Communist Party more executive control over the cabinet; Reuters said this continued a long transfer of power from state organs to the Party, and the premier’s post-parliament press conference was canceled. | Reuters | 2024-03-11 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/china-passes-law-granting-communist-party-more-control-over-cabinet-3331891 | 5B.2 |
| Against | The Party created a new financial-sector anti-graft committee and assigned it political supervision and “party building” duties, showing tighter Party control over finance rather than insulation for professional economic managers. | Reuters | 2024-07-24 | https://hk.marketscreener.com/news/latest/China-targets-financial-sector-with-party-led-anti-graft-committee-47453350/ | 5B.2 |
| Against | Xi’s anti-graft line still centered on catching “corrupt and disloyal” officials, which suggests loyalty enforcement remained embedded in economic governance rather than a purely meritocratic technocratic system. | Reuters | 2024-01-10 | https://hk.marketscreener.com/news/latest/China-watchdog-doubles-down-on-vow-to-heed-Xi-s-anti-graft-drive-45713924/ | 5B.2 |

**Search gap**
- I did **not** find reliable 2024 evidence that Xi appointed family members or business partners to top economic posts.
- The public record I found is mostly about **Party cadres, technocrats, and institutional control**, so the strongest conclusion is about **limited empowerment** rather than direct patronage via relatives or business associates.
